verses.1:1: And it happened after the death of Joshua that the sons of Israel inquired through the Lord, saying, "Who will go up for us against the Canaanites, leading the way to fight against them?"
verses.1:2: And the Lord said, "Judah will go up; look, I have given the land into his hand."
verses.1:3: And Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and let us engage in battle against the Canaanites, and I also will go with you into your lot." And Simeon went with him.
verses.1:4: And Judah went up, and the Lord delivered the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hands, and they cut them down in Bezek, up to ten thousand men.
verses.1:5: And they came upon Adoni-bezek in Bezek and engaged in battle against him, and they cut down the Canaanite and the Perizzite.
verses.1:6: And Adoni-bezek fled, and they chased after him and caught him, and they cut off the extremities of his hands and the extremities of his feet.
verses.1:7: And Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with the extremities of their hands and the extremities of their feet cut off were gathering what was underneath my table; therefore, just as I did, so God has repaid me." And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.1:8: And the sons of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and captured it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and burned the city with fire.
verses.1:9: And after these things the sons of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanite who lived in the hill country and the south and the plain.
verses.1:10: And Judah went against the Canaanite who lived in Hebron, and Hebron came out in opposition; and the name of Hebron formerly was Kariarboxepher. And they struck down Sheshai and Ahinaan and Talmai, offspring of Anak.
verses.1:11: And they went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir; now the name of Debir previously was Kiriath-sepher, City of Letters.
verses.1:12: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes the City of Letters and captures it, I will give him Aza my daughter as a wife."
verses.1:13: And Othniel the younger, the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, captured it; and Caleb gave him Aza his daughter as a wife.
verses.1:14: And it happened at her coming in that Othniel urged her to ask for a field from her father; and she murmured and cried out from the donkey, "You have given me away into a land of the south." And Caleb said to her, "What is the matter with you?"
verses.1:15: And Achsah said to him, "Please give me a blessing, because you have given me away into a land of the south, and you shall give me a redemption of water." And Caleb gave her, according to her heart, a redemption of high places and a redemption of low places.
verses.1:16: And the sons of Jethro the Kenite, the father-in-law of Moses, went up from the City of Palms with the sons of Judah into the wilderness that is in the south of Judah, which is at the descent of Arad. They lived with the people.
verses.1:17: And Judah went with Simeon his brother and cut down the Canaanite who lived in Sephek, and they utterly destroyed them; and he called the name of the city Anathema.
verses.1:18: And Judah did not inherit Gaza nor its borders, nor Ashkelon nor its borders, nor Ekron nor its borders, nor Ashdod nor its surrounding fields.
verses.1:19: And the Lord was with Judah, and he inherited the mountain, because they were not able to utterly destroy the inhabitants of the valley, because Rechab commanded them.
verses.1:20: And they gave Hebron to Caleb, just as Moses spoke; and he inherited from there the three cities of the sons of Anak.
verses.1:21: And the sons of Benjamin did not dispossess the Jebusite who lived in Jerusalem, and the Jebusite lived with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem until this day.
verses.1:22: And the sons of Joseph went up, they also, to Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
verses.1:23: And they encamped and spied out Bethel; now the name of their city previously was Luz.
verses.1:24: And the watchmen saw, and look, a man was coming out of the city; and they seized him and said to him, "Show us the entrance of the city, and we will show mercy to you."
verses.1:25: And he showed them the entrance of the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they sent the man and his relatives away.
verses.1:26: And the man went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city there and called its name Luz. This is its name until this day.
verses.1:27: And Manasseh did not remove Beth-shean, which is the City of the Scythians, nor its daughters nor its surrounding settlements, nor Taanach nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Dor nor its daughters, nor the inhabitant of Balak nor its surrounding settlements nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo nor its surrounding settlements nor its daughters, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam nor its surrounding settlements nor its daughters; and the Canaanite began to live in this land.
verses.1:28: And it happened when Israel grew strong that he made the Canaanite subject to tribute, and he did not completely remove him.
verses.1:29: And Ephraim did not remove the Canaanite who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanite lived in his midst in Gezer and became subject to tribute.
verses.1:30: And Zebulun did not remove the inhabitants of Kedron nor the inhabitants of Domana, and the Canaanite lived in their midst and became subject to tribute to him.
verses.1:31: And Asher did not remove the inhabitants of Acco (and it became subject to tribute to him), and the inhabitants of Dor, and the inhabitants of Sidon, and the inhabitants of Dalaph, Aschazei, and Chebda, and Naei, and Ereo.
verses.1:32: And Asher lived in the midst of the Canaanite who lived in the land, because he was not able to remove him.
verses.1:33: And Naphtali did not remove the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and the inhabitants of Beth-anath; and Naphtali lived in the midst of the Canaanite who lived in the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became subject to tribute to them.
verses.1:34: And the Amorite pressed the sons of Dan into the mountain, because they did not allow him to go down into the valley.
verses.1:35: And the Amorite began to live in the potsherd mountain, where the bears are and where the foxes are, in the Myrtle Grove and in Thalabin; and the hand of the house of Joseph grew heavy upon the Amorite, and he became subject to tribute to them.
verses.1:36: And the border of the Amorite was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the Rock and upward.
verses.2:1: And the angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to the Place of Weeping and to Bethel and to the house of Israel, and said to them, "Thus says the Lord: I brought you up out of Egypt and brought you into the land that I swore to your fathers, and I said, 'I will not break My covenant with you forever.
verses.2:2: And you shall not make a covenant with those who dwell in this land, nor shall you bow down to their gods, but you shall shatter their carved images, you shall tear down their altars.' Yet you did not listen to My voice, because you did these things.
verses.2:3: And I also said, 'I will certainly not remove them from before you, and they will become distresses to you, and their gods will become a snare to you.'"
verses.2:4: And it happened, when the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.2:5: And they called the name of that place Places of Weeping, and they sacrificed there to the Lord.
verses.2:6: And Joshua sent the people away, and each man went to his inheritance to inherit the land.
verses.2:7: And the people served the Lord all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who prolonged their days with Joshua, who knew all the great work of the Lord, all that He had done in Israel.
verses.2:8: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, one hundred ten years old.
verses.2:9: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in Mount Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.2:10: And all that generation also was added to their fathers; and another generation arose after them who did not know the Lord, nor even the work that He had done in Israel.
verses.2:11: And the sons of Israel did what was evil before the Lord, and served the Baals.
verses.2:12: And they abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and went after other gods from among the gods of the nations that were around them, and bowed down to them; and they provoked the Lord to anger.
verses.2:13: And they abandoned Him, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.2:14: And the Lord became angry with wrath against Israel, and delivered them into the hands of plunderers, and they thoroughly plundered them; and He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, and they were no longer able to stand before their enemies wherever they went out.
verses.2:15: And the hand of the Lord was against them for harm, just as the Lord had spoken, and just as the Lord had sworn to them, and He oppressed them greatly.
verses.2:16: And the Lord raised up judges, and the Lord saved them from the hand of those who plundered them. Yet they did not even obey the judges,
verses.2:17: because they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them, and turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked to listen to the words of the Lord; they did not do so.
verses.2:18: And when the Lord raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the Lord was moved to pity by their groaning on account of those who besieged them and oppressed them.
verses.2:19: And it happened, whenever the judge died, that they turned back and again acted more corruptly than their fathers, to go after other gods, to serve them and to bow down to them; they did not cast off their practices and their stubborn ways.
verses.2:20: And the Lord became angry with wrath against Israel and said, "Because this nation has abandoned My covenant that I commanded their fathers, and did not listen to My voice,
verses.2:21: I also will no longer remove a man from before them from the nations that Joshua the son of Nun left in the land." And He left them
verses.2:22: to test Israel by them, whether they keep the way of the Lord to walk in it, just as their fathers kept it, or not.
verses.2:23: And the Lord will leave these nations, so as not to remove them quickly, and He did not deliver them into the hand of Joshua.
verses.3:1: And these are the nations that the Lord left to test Israel by them, all those who had not known the wars of Canaan,
verses.3:2: only on account of the generations of the sons of Israel, to teach them war; only those before them did not know them:
verses.3:3: the five satrapies of the foreigners, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in Lebanon, from Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
verses.3:4: And it was to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the commandments of the Lord, which He commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
verses.3:5: And the sons of Israel lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.3:6: And they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and they gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
verses.3:7: And the sons of Israel did what was evil before the Lord, and they forgot the Lord their God, and they served the Baals and the groves.
verses.3:8: And the Lord was angry with fury against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of the rivers of Syria. And the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
verses.3:9: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up a savior for Israel, and he saved them: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, who was younger than him.
verses.3:10: And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel. And he went out to war against Cushan-rishathaim; and the Lord delivered Cushan-rishathaim, king of Syria of the rivers, into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
verses.3:11: And the land was at rest for forty years; and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
verses.3:12: And the sons of Israel again did what was evil before the Lord; and the Lord strengthened Eglon, king of Moab, against Israel, because they had done what was evil before the Lord.
verses.3:13: And he gathered to himself all the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and he took possession of the city of palm trees.
verses.3:14: And the sons of Israel served Eglon, king of Moab, eighteen years.
verses.3:15: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord; and He raised up for them a savior, Ehud the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, an ambidextrous man. And the sons of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglon, king of Moab.
verses.3:16: And Ehud made for himself a two-edged dagger, a span in its length, and he strapped it under his cloak on his right thigh.
verses.3:17: And he went and presented the gifts to Eglon, king of Moab; and Eglon was a very handsome man.
verses.3:18: And it happened, when Ehud had finished presenting the gifts, that he sent away those who carried the gifts.
verses.3:19: And he himself turned back from the carved images that were by Gilgal, and Ehud said, "I have a secret word for you, king." And Eglon said to him, "Be silent!" And he sent away from himself all those who stood beside him.
verses.3:20: And Ehud went in to him; and he was sitting in his own summer upper room completely alone. And Ehud said, "I have a word of God for you, king." And Eglon rose up from the throne near him.
verses.3:21: And it happened, at the very moment he rose up, that Ehud stretched out his left hand and took the dagger from off his right thigh and thrust it into his belly,
verses.3:22: and he drove even the hilt in after the flame; and the fat closed over the flame, for he did not pull the dagger out of his belly.
verses.3:23: And Ehud went out into the porch, and he went out past those who were stationed, and he closed the doors of the upper room upon him, and bolted them.
verses.3:24: And he went out; and his servants came and looked, and look, the doors of the upper room were bolted. And they said, "Is he perhaps emptying his feet in the summer chamber?"
verses.3:25: And they waited until they were embarrassed. And look, there was no one opening the doors of the upper room; so they took the key and opened them, and look, their lord had fallen on the ground, dead.
verses.3:26: And Ehud escaped while they were in confusion, and there was no one paying attention to him; and he passed by the carved images and escaped to Seteirotha.
verses.3:27: And it happened, when Ehud came into the land of Israel, that he sounded a horn in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he was in front of them.
verses.3:28: And he said to them, "Come down after me, for the Lord God has delivered our enemies, Moab, into our hand." And they went down after him, and they seized beforehand the fords of the Jordan of Moab, and he did not allow a man to cross over.
verses.3:29: And they struck Moab on that day, about ten thousand men, every stout one and every man of strength, and not a man escaped.
verses.3:30: And Moab was humbled on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land was at rest for eighty years; and Ehud judged them until he died.
verses.3:31: And after him rose up Shamgar the son of Dinach, and he struck down the foreigners, up to six hundred men, with the plowshare of the oxen, and he also saved Israel.
verses.4:1: And the sons of Israel again did what was evil before the Lord; and Ehud had died.
verses.4:2: And the Lord sold the sons of Israel into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; and the commander of his army was Sisera, and he lived in Harosheth of the nations.
verses.4:3: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, because he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed Israel forcefully for twenty years.
verses.4:4: And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, she was judging Israel at that time.
verses.4:5: And she sat under the palm tree of Deborah between Bama and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her for judgment.
verses.4:6: And Deborah sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and she said to him, "Has not the Lord, the God of Israel, commanded you, and you shall go to Mount Tabor, and you shall take with yourself ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun,
verses.4:7: and I will march to you to the torrent Kishon against Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will deliver him into your hands?"
verses.4:8: And Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go, and if you do not go, I will not go; for I do not know the day on which the Lord prospers the angel with me."
verses.4:9: And she said, "I will surely go with you; only know that your honor will not be on the way that you are going, for the Lord will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." And Deborah rose up and went with Barak from Kedesh.
verses.4:10: And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali from Kedesh, and ten thousand men went up at his feet; and Deborah went up with him.
verses.4:11: And Heber the Kenite had separated himself from Kain, from the sons of Jobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and he pitched his tent as far as the oak of the greedy, which is next to Kedesh.
verses.4:12: And it was reported to Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
verses.4:13: And Sisera called all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth of the nations to the torrent Kishon.
verses.4:14: And Deborah said to Barak, "Rise up, for this is the day on which the Lord has delivered Sisera into your hand, for the Lord will go out before you." And Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men were behind him.
verses.4:15: And the Lord threw Sisera and all his chariots and all his camp into panic with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on his feet.
verses.4:16: And Barak was pursuing after the chariots and after the camp as far as Harosheth of the nations; and all the camp of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not even one was left.
verses.4:17: And Sisera fled on his feet to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the companion, the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin, king of Hazor, and the house of Heber the Kenite.
verses.4:18: And Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid." And he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.4:19: And Sisera said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." And she opened the skin of milk and gave him a drink, and she covered him.
verses.4:20: And Sisera said to her, "Please stand at the door of the tent, and it will be, if a man comes to you and asks you and says, 'Is there a man here?' then you shall say, 'There is not.'"
verses.4:21: And Jael, the wife of Heber, took the tent peg and put the hammer in her hand, and she went in to him secretly and drove the peg into his temple, and it went right through into the ground; and he, stunned, fainted and died.
verses.4:22: And look, Barak was pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." And he went in to her, and look, Sisera lay cast down, dead, and the peg was in his temple.
verses.4:23: And on that day God routed Jabin, king of Canaan, before the sons of Israel.
verses.4:24: And the hand of the sons of Israel kept going on and growing harder against Jabin, king of Canaan, until they completely destroyed Jabin, king of Canaan.
verses.5:1: And Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam were saying on that day:
verses.5:2: "A revelation was revealed in Israel; when people were unwilling, bless the Lord.
verses.5:3: Hear, kings, and give ear, satraps: I am for the Lord; I myself will sing, I will sing praises to the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:4: Lord, at Your going forth in Seir, when You departed from the field of Edom, the earth shook, and heaven dripped dews, and the clouds dripped water.
verses.5:5: Mountains were shaken from the presence of the Lord Eloi, this Sinai from the presence of the Lord, the God of Israel.
verses.5:6: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, they abandoned roads and walked footpaths; they walked crooked roads.
verses.5:7: Mighty men failed in Israel, they failed, until Deborah arose, until a mother arose in Israel.
verses.5:8: They chose new gods when cities of rulers fought, if a shield should be seen and a spear among forty thousand in Israel.
verses.5:9: My heart is toward the things ordained for Israel; you who offer yourselves willingly among the people, bless the Lord.
verses.5:10: You who ride on a female donkey at midday, sitting on a judgment seat and walking on roads of councilors by the road.
verses.5:11: Recount from the sound of those playing music, in the midst of those drawing water; there they will give righteous deeds. Lord, increase righteous deeds in Israel; then the people of the Lord went down to the cities.
verses.5:12: Awake, awake, Deborah; awake, awake, speak a song. Arise, Barak, and take captive your captivity, son of Abinoam.
verses.5:13: Then a remnant went down for the strong; the people of the Lord went down for Him among the mighty from me.
verses.5:14: Ephraim uprooted them in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. In me, Machir went down searching out, and from Zebulun, those drawing with a staff of a scribe's account.
verses.5:15: And leaders in Issachar were with Deborah and Barak. So Barak sent forth in valleys at his feet. For the portions of Reuben, great ones reaching the heart.
verses.5:16: Why did they sit between the double load to hear the piping of messengers? For the divisions of Reuben, great searchings of heart.
verses.5:17: Gilead camped beyond the Jordan; and Dan, why does he sojourn by ships? Asher sat on the coast of the seas, and at his outlets he will camp.
verses.5:18: Zebulun is a people that scorned its life to death, and Naphtali on the heights of the field.
verses.5:19: Their kings came, they did battle; then the kings of Canaan fought in Taanach by the water of Megiddo; they did not take a gift of silver.
verses.5:20: From heaven the stars did battle; from their paths they did battle with Sisera.
verses.5:21: The torrent of Kishon swept them away, the torrent of ancient ones, the torrent of Kishon; my mighty soul will trample him down.
verses.5:22: Then the heels of a horse were entangled; in haste his strong ones hastened.
verses.5:23: 'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the Lord, 'curse; cursed is everyone who inhabits it, because they did not come to the help of the Lord, to help among the mighty.'
verses.5:24: May Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, be blessed among women; above women in tents may she be blessed.
verses.5:25: Water he asked for, milk she gave; in a bowl of nobles she brought butter.
verses.5:26: Her left hand she stretched out to a peg, and her right hand to a hammer of laborers; and she hammered Sisera, pierced through his head and struck, pierced through his temple.
verses.5:27: Between her feet he rolled down, he fell and lay down between her feet; sinking down, he fell; just as he sank down, there he fell, undone.
verses.5:28: Through the window the mother of Sisera peered out beyond the arrow-slit: 'Why was his chariot put to shame? Why have the feet of his chariots delayed?'
verses.5:29: Her wise princesses answered her, and she returned her words to herself:
verses.5:30: 'Will they not find him dividing spoil? A compassionate one will show compassion for the head of a man; spoil of dyed fabrics for Sisera, spoil of dyed fabrics of embroidery, dyed fabrics of embroiderers are these, for his neck, spoil.'
verses.5:31: So may all Your enemies perish, Lord; and may those who love Him be like the going forth of the sun in its power." And the land was quiet forty years.
verses.6:1: And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
verses.6:2: And the hand of Midian prevailed over Israel; and because of Midian the sons of Israel made for themselves the crevices that are in the mountains, and the caves, and the steep places.
verses.6:3: And it happened whenever the sons of Israel sowed, Midian and Amalek would come up, and the sons of the east would come up with them; and they encamped against them,
verses.6:4: and they destroyed their produce as far as coming to Gaza, and they did not leave sustenance of life in the land of Israel, nor among the flocks a bull and a donkey.
verses.6:5: For they and their livestock would come up, and their tents would arrive like locusts in multitude, and for them and their camels there was no number; and they would come into the land of Israel and destroy it,
verses.6:6: and Israel became exceedingly poor because of Midian.
verses.6:7: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord because of Midian.
verses.6:8: And the Lord sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am the One who brought you up from the land of Egypt, and I brought you out from the house of your slavery,
verses.6:9: and I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and I drove them out from before you, and I gave you their land;
verses.6:10: and I said to you, 'I am the Lord your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorite, among whom you will dwell in their land.' And you did not listen to My voice."
verses.6:11: And the angel of the Lord came and sat under the terebinth that was in Ephrathah, in what belonged to Joash, father of Esdri; and Gideon his son was beating out wheat in a winepress in order to escape from before Midian.
verses.6:12: And the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said to him, "The Lord is with you, mighty one of powers."
verses.6:13: And Gideon said to him, "In me, my lord, and if the Lord is with us, why have these evils found us? And where are all His wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt?' And now He has cast us off and given us into the hand of Midian."
verses.6:14: And the angel of the Lord turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and you will save Israel from the hand of Midian; look, I have sent you."
verses.6:15: And Gideon said to him, "In me, my lord, with what shall I save Israel? Look, my thousand has grown weak in Manasseh, and I am the least in the house of my father."
verses.6:16: And the angel of the Lord said to him, "The Lord will be with you, and you will strike Midian as one man."
verses.6:17: And Gideon said to him, "Now if I have found mercy in your eyes, and you will do for me today everything that you have spoken with me,
verses.6:18: do not depart from here until I come to you; and I will bring out the offering and set it before you." And he said, "I myself will sit until you return."
verses.6:19: And Gideon went in and prepared a kid of goats and an ephah of flour, unleavened cakes, and he put the meat in the basket and put the broth in the pot, and he brought them out to him under the terebinth, and came near.
verses.6:20: And the angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and place them by that rock, and pour out the broth close by." And he did so.
verses.6:21: And the angel of the Lord stretched out the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes, and fire came up out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes; and the angel of the Lord went away from his eyes.
verses.6:22: And Gideon saw that he was the angel of the Lord; and Gideon said, "Ah, ah, my Lord, Lord, for I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face!"
verses.6:23: And the Lord said to him, "Peace to you; do not fear, you will certainly not die."
verses.6:24: And Gideon built an altar there to the Lord and called it "Peace of the Lord"; to this day it is still in Ephrathah of the father of Esdri.
verses.6:25: And it happened on that night that the Lord said to him, "Take the bull calf that belongs to your father, and a second calf seven years old, and you shall tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and you shall destroy the grove that is by it;
verses.6:26: and you shall build an altar to the Lord your God on the top of this Mauek in the ordered arrangement, and you shall take the second calf and offer up a burnt offering with the wood of the grove that you will utterly destroy."
verses.6:27: And Gideon took ten men from his own servants and did just as the Lord had spoken to him; and it happened, because he was too afraid of the house of his father and the men of the city to do it by day, that he did it by night.
verses.6:28: And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and look, the altar of Baal had been torn down, and the grove that was by it had been destroyed; and they saw the second calf, which he had offered up on the altar that had been built.
verses.6:29: And each man said to his neighbor, "Who has done this thing?" And they inquired and investigated, and they learned that Gideon son of Joash had done this thing.
verses.6:30: And the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son and let him die, because he tore down the altar of Baal, and because he destroyed the grove that was by it."
verses.6:31: And Gideon son of Joash said to all the men who rose up against him, "Are you now contending for Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him, let him be put to death by morning; if he is a god, let him contend for himself, because he tore down his altar."
verses.6:32: And he called it Arbaal on that day, saying, "Let Baal contend against him, because his altar was torn down."
verses.6:33: And all Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east were gathered together, and they encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
verses.6:34: And the Spirit of the Lord empowered Gideon, and he blew a horn, and Abiezer was afraid after him.
verses.6:35: And he sent messengers into all Manasseh, and into Asher, and into Zebulun and Naphtali, and he went up to meet them.
verses.6:36: And Gideon said to God, "If You are saving Israel by my hand, just as You have spoken,
verses.6:37: look, I am placing the fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if dew is on the fleece alone and dryness on all the ground, I will know that You will save Israel by my hand, just as You have spoken."
verses.6:38: And it was so; and he rose early the next day and squeezed out the fleece, and dew dripped from the fleece, a full bowl of water.
verses.6:39: And Gideon said to God, "Please do not let Your anger be provoked against me, and I will speak once more; let me test even once more with the fleece, and let the dryness be on the fleece alone, and on all the ground let there be dew."
verses.6:40: And God did so on that night; and there was dryness on the fleece alone, and on all the ground there was dew.
verses.7:1: And Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, and all the people with him rose early, and they camped by the spring of Harod; and the camp of Midian was north of him, from Gabaathamora in the valley.
verses.7:2: And the Lord said to Gideon, "The people with you are too many for Me to deliver Midian into their hand, so that Israel will not boast against Me, saying, 'My hand saved me.'
verses.7:3: And now speak in the ears of the people, saying, 'Who is fearful and timid? Let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.'" And twenty-two thousand from the people turned back, and ten thousand were left.
verses.7:4: And the Lord said to Gideon, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there; and it will be that the one of whom I say to you, 'This one will go with you,' he will go with you; and everyone of whom I say to you, 'This one will not go with you,' he will not go with you."
verses.7:5: And he brought the people down to the water; and the Lord said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps from the water with his tongue as a dog laps, you will set him by himself, and everyone who bows down on his knees to drink."
verses.7:6: And the number of those who lapped with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men, and all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water.
verses.7:7: And the Lord said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand, and all the people will go, each man to his place."
verses.7:8: And they took the provisions of the people in their hand and their horns; and he sent away all the men of Israel, each man to his tent, and he retained the three hundred men. And the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
verses.7:9: And it happened on that night that the Lord said to him, "Rise, go down against the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.
verses.7:10: And if you are afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your servant, to the camp,
verses.7:11: and you will hear what they will say; and after this your hands will be strong, and you will go down against the camp." And he and Purah his servant went down to the edge of the fifty who were in the camp.
verses.7:12: Now Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the east were lying in the valley like locusts in multitude, and their camels were without number; rather, they were like the sand on the shore of the sea in multitude.
verses.7:13: And Gideon came, and look, a man was relating a dream to his companion, and he said, "See, I dreamed a dream, and look, a cake of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian, and it came up to the tent and struck it, and it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent fell."
verses.7:14: And his companion answered and said, "This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel; God has delivered Midian and all the camp into his hand."
verses.7:15: And it happened, when Gideon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation, that he worshiped the Lord; and he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Rise, for the Lord has delivered the camp of Midian into our hand."
verses.7:16: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put horns into the hand of all of them, and empty water jars, and torches inside the jars.
verses.7:17: And he said to them, "Look at me, and so you will do; and see, I am going in at the edge of the camp, and it will be that just as I do, so you will do.
verses.7:18: And I myself will blow the horn, and all of you with me will blow the horns around the entire camp, and you will say, 'For the Lord and for Gideon.'"
verses.7:19: And Gideon and the one hundred men who were with him went in at the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch; and they indeed roused the guards, and they blew the horns and shook out the water jars that were in their hands.
verses.7:20: And the three companies blew the horns and shattered the water jars, and they held the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands to blow, and they cried out, "A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!"
verses.7:21: And they stood, each man in his place, around the camp; and all the camp ran, and they sounded the alarm and fled.
verses.7:22: And they blew the three hundred horns, and the Lord set each man's sword against his companion throughout the entire camp; and the camp fled as far as Bethseedta Garagatha, as far as the edge of Abomeoula by Tabbath.
verses.7:23: And the men of Israel cried out from Naphtali and from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.
verses.7:24: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian, and seize for yourselves the water as far as Bethera and the Jordan." And every man of Ephraim cried out, and they seized the water beforehand as far as Bethera and the Jordan.
verses.7:25: And they captured the leaders of Midian, both Oreb and Zeeb, and they killed Oreb at Sur, and Zeeb they killed at Jakephzeph; and they pursued Midian, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from beyond the Jordan.
verses.8:1: And the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "What is this thing you have done to us, in not calling us when you went to do battle against Midian?" And they argued with him strongly.
verses.8:2: And he said to them, "What have I done now compared with you? Is not the gleaning of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
verses.8:3: Into your hand the Lord has delivered the leaders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what was I able to do compared with you?" Then their spirit subsided toward him when he spoke this word.
verses.8:4: And Gideon came to the Jordan, and he crossed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, hungry and pursuing.
verses.8:5: And he said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread for food to these people who are at my feet, for they are fainting, and look, I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian."
verses.8:6: And the leaders of Succoth said, "Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand? We will not give loaves of bread to your force."
verses.8:7: And Gideon said, "For this reason, when the Lord gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the habarkenein."
verses.8:8: And he went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
verses.8:9: And Gideon said to the men of Penuel, "When I return in peace, I will demolish this tower."
verses.8:10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their camp was with them, about fifteen thousand, all who were left from the entire camp of the foreigners; and those who had fallen were one hundred twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.8:11: And Gideon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents, east of Nabai and Jegebal; and he struck the camp, while the camp was feeling secure.
verses.8:12: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued after them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the entire camp into panic.
verses.8:13: And Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle, from above the battle of Heres.
verses.8:14: And he captured a young man from the men of Succoth and questioned him; and he wrote down for him the names of the leaders of Succoth and of their elders, seventy-seven men.
verses.8:15: And Gideon came to the leaders of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Is the hand of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give loaves of bread to the men who are fainting?'"
verses.8:16: And he took the elders of the city with the thorns of the wilderness and the barakeneim, and threshed the men of the city with them.
verses.8:17: And he tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
verses.8:18: And he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "Where are the men whom you killed at Tabor?" And they said, "As you are, so were they, in the likeness of a king's son."
verses.8:19: And Gideon said, "They were my brothers and the sons of my mother; as the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you."
verses.8:20: And he said to Jether his firstborn, "Rise, kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, for he was still very young.
verses.8:21: And Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise yourself and fall upon us, for your strength is like that of a man." So Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:22: And the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Master, rule over us, both you and your son, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian."
verses.8:23: And Gideon said to them, "I will not rule, and my son will not rule over you; the Lord will rule over you."
verses.8:24: And Gideon said to them, "I will make a request of you: let each man give me an earring from his plunder." For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
verses.8:25: And they said, "We will surely give them." And he spread out his garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder there.
verses.8:26: And the weight of the gold earrings that he requested was one thousand five hundred gold pieces, besides the crescent ornaments and the necklaces and the garments and purple robes that were on the kings of Midian, and apart from the collars that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:27: And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, Ephrathah; and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.
verses.8:28: And Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not lift up their heads again. And the land was quiet for forty years in the days of Gideon.
verses.8:29: And Jerubbaal son of Joash went and lived in his house.
verses.8:30: And Gideon had seventy sons who came from his loins, for he had many wives.
verses.8:31: And his concubine was in Shechem; and she also bore him a son, and he gave him the name Abimelech.
verses.8:32: And Gideon son of Joash died in his city, and he was buried in the tomb of Joash his father in Ephrathah of the Abiezrites.
verses.8:33: And it happened, as soon as Gideon died, that the sons of Israel turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and they made a covenant for themselves with Baal, so that he would be a god to them.
verses.8:34: And the sons of Israel did not remember the Lord God, who had rescued them from the hand of all who oppressed them all around;
verses.8:35: and they did not show mercy to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, according to all the good things that he had done for Israel.
verses.9:1: And Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother's brothers, and he spoke to them and to all the clan of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.9:2: "Please speak in the ears of all the men of Shechem, 'What is better for you: for seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, to rule over you, or for one man to rule over you? And remember that I am your bone and your flesh.'"
verses.9:3: And his mother's brothers spoke all these words about him in the ears of all the men of Shechem; and their heart inclined after Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
verses.9:4: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith, and Abimelech hired for himself worthless and cowardly men, and they went after him.
verses.9:5: And he went into his father's house at Ephrathah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone; yet Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left, because he hid himself.
verses.9:6: And all the men of Shechem and all the house of Beth-maalon gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king by the found oak of the station that was in Shechem.
verses.9:7: And it was reported to Jotham; and he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice and wept, and said to them, "Listen to me, men of Shechem, and God will listen to you.
verses.9:8: Going, the trees went to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
verses.9:9: And the olive tree said to them, 'Should I leave my richness, by which men will glorify God, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:10: And the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, reign over us.'
verses.9:11: And the fig tree said to them, 'Should I leave my sweetness and my good fruits and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:12: And the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you reign over us.'
verses.9:13: And the vine said to them, 'Should I leave my wine that gladdens God and people and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:14: And all the trees said to the bramble, 'Come, you reign over us.'
verses.9:15: And the bramble said to the trees, 'If in truth you are anointing me to reign over you, come, take shelter in my shadow; and if not, let fire come out from me and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
verses.9:16: And now, if you have acted in truth and integrity and have made Abimelech king, and if you have done good to Jerubbaal and to his house, and if you have done to him according to the repayment of his hand—
verses.9:17: since my father fought for you, and cast his life out in front, and rescued you from the hand of Midian,
verses.9:18: yet you have risen up against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his female servant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother—
verses.9:19: and if you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house on this day, may you rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice over you.
verses.9:20: But if not, may fire come out from Abimelech and consume the men of Shechem and the house of Beth-maalon, and may fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the house of Beth-maalon and devour Abimelech."
verses.9:21: And Jotham fled and escaped, and went as far as Beer and lived there, away from the presence of his brother Abimelech.
verses.9:22: And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
verses.9:23: And God sent out an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and the men of Shechem acted treacherously against the house of Abimelech,
verses.9:24: in order to bring the wrong done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal and their blood, to place them upon their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and upon the men of Shechem, because they strengthened his hands to kill the brothers.
verses.9:25: And the men of Shechem set ambushers against him on the tops of the mountains, and they were plundering everyone who passed by them on the road; and it was reported to King Abimelech.
verses.9:26: And Gilead son of Jobel and his brothers came and passed into Shechem, and the men of Shechem trusted in him.
verses.9:27: And they went out into the field and harvested their vineyards and trod them, and made helloulim, and brought them into the house of their god, and ate and spoke and cursed Abimelech.
verses.9:28: And Gaad son of Jobel said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is the son of Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul, his overseer, his servant with the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem? And why should we serve him?
verses.9:29: And who would give this people into my hand? Then I will remove Abimelech, and I will say to him, 'Increase your army and come out!'"
verses.9:30: And Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gilead son of Jobel, and he himself became furious with anger.
verses.9:31: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in secret, saying, "Look, Gilead son of Jobel and his brothers are coming to Shechem, and look, they are besieging the city against you.
verses.9:32: And now, rise up by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in ambush in the field;
verses.9:33: and it will be in the morning, as soon as the sun rises, you will rise early and advance against the city; and look, he and the people who are with him are coming out against you, and you will do to him whatever your hand finds."
verses.9:34: And Abimelech and all the people with him rose up by night, and they lay in ambush against Shechem in four companies.
verses.9:35: And Gilead son of Jobel went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and Abimelech and the people who were with him rose up from the ambush.
verses.9:36: And Gilead son of Jobel saw the people, and he said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as men."
verses.9:37: And Gilead spoke yet again and said, "Look, people are coming down toward the sea from next to the navel of the land, and another company is coming by the way of Elon-maonemin."
verses.9:38: And Zebul said to him, "And where is your mouth, as you spoke, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people whom you despised? Come out now and fight against him!"
verses.9:39: And Gilead went out before the men of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
verses.9:40: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from before him; and many wounded fell as far as the entrance of the gate.
verses.9:41: And Abimelech entered Arumah; and Zebul drove out Gilead and his brothers from living in Shechem.
verses.9:42: And it happened on the next day that the people went out into the field, and someone reported it to Abimelech.
verses.9:43: And he took the people and divided them into three companies, and lay in ambush in the field; and he looked, and see, the people came out from the city, and he rose up against them and struck them down.
verses.9:44: And Abimelech and the leaders who were with him advanced and stood beside the entrance of the gate of the city, and the two companies advanced against all who were in the field and struck them down.
verses.9:45: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people who were in it; and he tore down the city and sowed it with salt.
verses.9:46: And all the men of the towers of Shechem heard, and they came into the assembly place of Beth-er-berith.
verses.9:47: And it was reported to Abimelech that all the men of the towers of Shechem had gathered together.
verses.9:48: And Abimelech went up to Mount Hermon, and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took the axes in his hand, and cut off a branch of a tree and lifted it and placed it on his shoulders, and he said to the people who were with him, "What you saw me doing, quickly do as I did."
verses.9:49: And each one, every man, also cut off a branch, and they went after Abimelech and placed them upon the assembly place, and burned the assembly place over them with fire; and all the men of the tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.
verses.9:50: And Abimelech went from Beth-er-berith and encamped against Thebez, and he captured it.
verses.9:51: And there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and the women of the city fled there, and shut it on the outside of them, and went up onto the roof of the tower.
verses.9:52: And Abimelech came as far as the tower, and they fought against him; and Abimelech drew near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
verses.9:53: And a certain woman threw a piece of an upper millstone onto Abimelech's head, and broke his skull.
verses.9:54: And he cried out quickly to the young man who carried his armor and said to him, "Draw my sword and put me to death, so that they do not say, 'A woman killed him.'" And his young man pierced him through, and he died.
verses.9:55: And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, and they went, each man to his place.
verses.9:56: And God returned the wickedness of Abimelech, which he had done to his father in killing his seventy brothers.
verses.9:57: And all the wickedness of the men of Shechem God returned upon their head, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
verses.10:1: And after Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of his paternal uncle, a man of Issachar, rose up to save Israel; and he lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.10:2: And he judged Israel twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir.
verses.10:3: And after him, Jair of Gilead rose up, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
verses.10:4: And he had thirty-two sons riding on thirty-two colts, and they had thirty-two cities; and they called them Settlements of Jair to this day, in the land of Gilead.
verses.10:5: And Jair died and was buried in Ramnon.
verses.10:6: And the sons of Israel again did what was evil before the Lord, and they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Arad, and the gods of Sidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the sons of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they abandoned the Lord and did not serve Him.
verses.10:7: And the Lord was angry with wrath against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:8: And they afflicted and crushed the sons of Israel at that time for eighteen years, all the sons of Israel who were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites who were in Gilead.
verses.10:9: And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to do battle against Judah and Benjamin and against Ephraim; and Israel was severely afflicted.
verses.10:10: And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, "We have sinned against You, because we have abandoned God and have served the Baals."
verses.10:11: And the Lord said to the sons of Israel, "Was it not from Egypt, and from the Amorites, and from the sons of Ammon, and from the Philistines,
verses.10:12: and the Sidonians, and Amalek, and Midian, who afflicted you; and you cried out to Me, and I saved you out of their hand?
verses.10:13: Yet you abandoned Me and served other gods; therefore I will not save you again.
verses.10:14: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen for yourselves, and let them save you in the time of your affliction."
verses.10:15: And the sons of Israel said to the Lord, "We have sinned; do to us Yourself according to all that is good in Your eyes; only deliver us on this day."
verses.10:16: And they put away the foreign gods from their midst and served the Lord alone; and His soul was distressed over the misery of Israel.
verses.10:17: And the sons of Ammon went up and encamped in Gilead, and the sons of Israel gathered together and encamped at the watchtower.
verses.10:18: And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said, each man to his neighbor, "Who is the man who will begin to do battle against the sons of Ammon? He will be leader over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
verses.11:1: And Jephthah the Gileadite was exalted in strength; and he was the son of a prostitute, who bore Jephthah to Gilead.
verses.11:2: And the wife of Gilead bore sons to him; and the sons of the wife grew up, and they drove out Jephthah and said to him, "You will not inherit in the house of our father, because you are the son of a courtesan."
verses.11:3: And Jephthah fled from before his brothers and lived in the land of Tob; and worthless men gathered to Jephthah and went out with him.
verses.11:4: And it happened, when the sons of Ammon did battle with Israel,
verses.11:5: that the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.
verses.11:6: And they said to Jephthah, "Come, and you will be commander over us, and let us do battle against the sons of Ammon."
verses.11:7: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me, and drive me out of my father's house, and send me away from you? And why have you come to me now when you are in need?"
verses.11:8: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "For this reason we have now returned to you, and you will go with us and do battle against the sons of Ammon, and you will be leader over us, over all who live in Gilead."
verses.11:9: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to do battle against the sons of Ammon, and the Lord delivers them before me, then will I be leader over you?"
verses.11:10: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "May the Lord be listening between us if we do not do so according to your word."
verses.11:11: And Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as head and as commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the Lord in Mizpah.
verses.11:12: And Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, "What is there between me and you, that you have come to me to do battle in my land?"
verses.11:13: And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthah, "Because Israel took my land when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok and to the Jordan; and now return them in peace, and I will go."
verses.11:14: And Jephthah once again sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:15: And he said to him, "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:16: For when they came up out of Egypt, Israel went in the wilderness as far as the Sea of Siph, and came to Kadesh.
verses.11:17: And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let me pass through your land.' And the king of Edom did not listen; and he sent to the king of Moab, and he did not consent. And Israel stayed in Kadesh.
verses.11:18: And he went in the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab; and he came from the rising of the sun to the land of Moab, and they encamped beyond the Arnon, and he did not enter into the borders of Moab, for the Arnon is the border of Moab.
verses.11:19: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to our place.'
verses.11:20: And Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; and Sihon gathered all his people together, and they encamped at Jahaz, and he did battle against Israel.
verses.11:21: And the Lord God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and he struck him; and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived in that land,
verses.11:22: from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
verses.11:23: And now the Lord God of Israel has removed the Amorites from before His people Israel, and will you possess them?
verses.11:24: Will you not possess whatever Hamos your god gives you to possess? And all those whom the Lord our God has removed from before us, them we will possess.
verses.11:25: And now, are you any better at all than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever wage war against him
verses.11:26: while they lived in Heshbon and in its territories, and in the land of Aroer and in its territories, and in all the cities that are beside the Jordan, for three hundred years? And why did you not rescue them at that time?
verses.11:27: And now I myself have not sinned against you, yet you are doing evil toward me by doing battle against me. May the Lord, the Judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon."
verses.11:28: And the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words of Jephthah that he had sent to him.
verses.11:29: And the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and he passed through the watchtower of Gilead to the region beyond the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:30: And Jephthah vowed a vow to the Lord and said, "If You indeed give the sons of Ammon into my hand,
verses.11:31: then the one coming out, whoever comes out from the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon, will belong to the Lord; I will offer him up as a burnt offering."
verses.11:32: And Jephthah crossed over to the sons of Ammon to do battle against them, and the Lord delivered them into his hand.
verses.11:33: And he struck them from Aroer until one comes to Arnon, twenty cities in number, and as far as Abel-keramim, with a very great slaughter; and the sons of Ammon were subdued before the sons of Israel.
verses.11:34: And Jephthah came to Mizpah, to his house, and look, his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and dances; and she was an only child; he had no other son or daughter.
verses.11:35: And it happened, when he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, "Ah, ah, my daughter! You have greatly troubled me, and you were in my trouble; and I myself have opened my mouth against you to the Lord, and I will not be able to turn back."
verses.11:36: And she said to him, "Father, you have opened your mouth to the Lord; do to me just as has gone out from your mouth, since the Lord has executed vengeance for you on your enemies, on the sons of Ammon."
verses.11:37: And she said to her father, "Please let my father do this thing: leave me alone for two months, and I will go and go down upon the mountains, and I will weep over my virginity, I myself and my companions."
verses.11:38: And he said, "Go." And he sent her away for two months. And she went, she and her companions, and wept over her virginity upon the mountains.
verses.11:39: And it happened at the end of the two months that she returned to her father, and he carried out on her his vow that he had vowed; and she did not know a man. And it became an ordinance in Israel:
verses.11:40: Year by year the daughters of Israel would go to lament the daughter of Jephthah of Gilead for four days in the year.
verses.12:1: And the men of Ephraim cried out, and crossed over to the north, and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to do battle against the sons of Ammon, and have not called us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire."
verses.12:2: And Jephthah said to them, "I was a fighting man, I and my people and the sons of Ammon, exceedingly; and I cried out to you, and you did not save me from their hand.
verses.12:3: And I saw that you are not a savior, and I placed my life in my hand and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord gave them into my hand. And why have you come up against me on this day to do battle against me?"
verses.12:4: And Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and did battle against Ephraim; and the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because the survivors of Ephraim said, "You are Gilead in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasseh."
verses.12:5: And Gilead seized beforehand the fords of the Jordan of Ephraim. And the survivors of Ephraim said to them, "Let us cross over." And the men of Gilead said to them, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he said, "No."
verses.12:6: And they said to him, "Say now, 'Ear of grain.'" And he did not manage to speak that way, and they seized him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time from Ephraim forty-two thousand.
verses.12:7: And Jephthah judged Israel sixty years. And Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in his city in Gilead.
verses.12:8: And after him Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel.
verses.12:9: And he had thirty sons and thirty daughters, whom he sent outside, and thirty daughters he brought in for his sons from outside. And he judged Israel seven years.
verses.12:10: And Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
verses.12:11: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel ten years.
verses.12:12: And Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Elon in the land of Zebulun.
verses.12:13: And after him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
verses.12:14: And he had forty sons and thirty grandsons, riding on seventy colts. And he judged Israel eight years.
verses.12:15: And Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of Amalek.
verses.13:1: And the sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
verses.13:2: And there was a certain man from Saral, from the clan of the family of the Danites, and his name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had not given birth.
verses.13:3: And the angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her, "Look, you are barren and have not given birth, and you will conceive a son.
verses.13:4: And now be careful, and do not drink wine or intoxicating drink, and do not eat anything unclean;
verses.13:5: for look, you are with child and will bear a son, and no iron shall come up upon his head, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from the womb; and he himself will begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.13:6: And the woman went in and spoke to her husband, saying, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of God, exceedingly fearsome; and I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.
verses.13:7: And he said to me, 'Look, you are with child and will bear a son. And now do not drink wine or intoxicating drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy will be a holy one of God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
verses.13:8: And Manoah prayed to the Lord and said, "Please, Lord Adonai, may the man of God whom You sent come to us once more, and instruct us what we should do for the child who is to be born."
verses.13:9: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman; and she was sitting in the field, and Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.13:10: And the woman hurried and ran and told her husband, and said to him, "Look, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me."
verses.13:11: And Manoah arose and went after his wife, and came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And the angel said, "I am."
verses.13:12: And Manoah said, "Now your word will come to pass. What will be the rule for the child and his deeds?"
verses.13:13: And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, "She shall guard herself from all that I have spoken to the woman.
verses.13:14: She shall not eat of anything that comes from the vine of wine, and let her not drink wine or strong intoxicating drink, and let her not eat anything unclean; all that I commanded him she shall observe."
verses.13:15: And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, "Let us detain you here, and let us prepare before you a kid of the goats."
verses.13:16: And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, "If you detain me, I will not eat of your bread; and if you prepare a burnt offering, you shall offer it up to the Lord." For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the Lord.
verses.13:17: And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, "What is your name? For may your word come to pass, and we will honor you."
verses.13:18: And the angel of the Lord said to him, "Why is it that you ask my name? And it is wonderful."
verses.13:19: And Manoah took the kid of the goats and the sacrifice and offered them up on the rock to the Lord, and He did a distinct thing, and Manoah and his wife were watching.
verses.13:20: And it happened when the flame went up above the altar to heaven, that the angel of the Lord went up in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.13:21: And the angel of the Lord did not appear again to Manoah and to his wife; then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the Lord.
verses.13:22: And Manoah said to his wife, "We will surely die, because we have seen God."
verses.13:23: And his wife said to him, "If the Lord had desired to put us to death, He would not have received a burnt offering and a sacrifice from our hand, and He would not have shown us all these things, and at such a time He would not have made us hear these things."
verses.13:24: And the woman bore a son and called his name Samson. And the boy grew up, and the Lord blessed him.
verses.13:25: And the Spirit of the Lord began to go out with him in the camp of Dan, and between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.14:1: And Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the foreigners.
verses.14:2: And he went up and told his father and his mother and said, "I have seen a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines; and now, take her for me as a wife."
verses.14:3: And his father and his mother said to him, "Are there not daughters of your brothers, and a woman from all my people, that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised foreigners?" And Samson said to his father, "Take this one for me, because she is right in my eyes."
verses.14:4: And his father and his mother did not know that it was from the Lord, for He Himself was seeking vengeance from the foreigners. And at that time the foreigners were ruling in Israel.
verses.14:5: And Samson and his father and his mother went down to Timnah; and he came as far as the vineyard of Timnah, and look, a young lion was roaring to meet him.
verses.14:6: And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he crushed it as one crushes a young goat, and there was nothing in his hands. And he did not tell his father and his mother what he had done.
verses.14:7: And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
verses.14:8: And he returned after some days to take her; and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and look, a swarm of bees was in the mouth of the lion, and honey.
verses.14:9: And he took it out into his hands, and went along, walking and eating; and he went to his father and his mother, and gave to them, and they ate, and he did not tell them that he had taken the honey out from the mouth of the lion.
verses.14:10: And his father went down to the woman; and Samson made a drinking feast there for seven days, for so the young men do.
verses.14:11: And it happened when they saw him, that they took thirty invited guests, and they were with him.
verses.14:12: And Samson said to them, "I propose a riddle to you: if you surely tell it within the seven days of the drinking feast and find it out, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty robes of clothing;
verses.14:13: and if you are not able to tell me, you yourselves shall give me thirty linen cloths and thirty changes of robes of clothing." And they said to him, "Propose the riddle, and we will hear it."
verses.14:14: And he said to them, "What edible thing came out from an eater, and from a strong one, what sweet thing?" And they were not able to tell the riddle for three days.
verses.14:15: And it happened on the fourth day that they said to Samson's wife, "Now deceive your husband and let him tell you the riddle, so that we do not burn you and your father's house with fire. Or have you invited us to force us out?"
verses.14:16: And Samson's wife wept before him and said, "You only hate me and have not loved me, because you have not told me the riddle that you proposed to the sons of my people." And Samson said to her, "If I have not told my father and my mother, shall I tell you?"
verses.14:17: And she wept before him for the seven days during which they had the drinking feast; and it happened on the seventh day that he told her, because she harassed him; and she told the sons of her people.
verses.14:18: And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun rose, "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" And Samson said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have known my riddle."
verses.14:19: And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men from among them, and took their garments, and gave the robes to those who had told the riddle. And Samson was enraged with fury, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.14:20: And Samson's wife came to belong to one of his friends whom he had befriended.
verses.15:1: And it came about after some days, in the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a kid of goats, and he said, "I will go in to my wife into the inner room." But her father did not allow him to go in.
verses.15:2: And her father said, "I truly said that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to one from among your friends. Is not her sister, who is younger than her, better than she is? Please let her be yours instead of her."
verses.15:3: And Samson said to them, "I am blameless even this once regarding foreigners, because I am doing evil to them."
verses.15:4: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and placed one torch between the two tails and bound them.
verses.15:5: And he kindled fire in the torches and sent them out into the ears of grain of the foreigners; and they were burned from threshing floor even to upright ears of grain, and even to vineyard and olive tree.
verses.15:6: And the foreigners said, "Who did these things?" And they said, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to the one from among his friends." And the foreigners went up and burned her and her father with fire.
verses.15:7: And Samson said to them, "If you act like this toward her, surely I will take vengeance on you, and afterward I will cease."
verses.15:8: And he struck them shin upon thigh, a great blow; and he went down and settled in a cleft of the rock of Etam.
verses.15:9: And the foreigners went up and encamped in Judah, and they were spread out in Lehi.
verses.15:10: And the men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" And the foreigners said, "We have come up to bind Samson, and to do to him just as he did to us."
verses.15:11: And three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and they said to Samson, "Do you not know that the foreigners will rule over us? And what is this that you have done to us?" And Samson said to them, "Just as they did to me, so I did to them."
verses.15:12: And they said to him, "We have come down to bind you, to give you into the hand of foreigners." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will never fall upon me."
verses.15:13: And they spoke to him, saying, "No, rather we will certainly bind you and deliver you into their hand, and we will certainly not put you to death." And they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from that rock.
verses.15:14: And they came as far as Jawbone, and the foreigners shouted and ran to meet him. And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that was burned in fire, and his bonds melted away from his hands.
verses.15:15: And he found a jawbone of a donkey that had been cast aside, and he stretched out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men with it.
verses.15:16: And Samson said, "With a jawbone of a donkey I utterly wiped them out, for with the jawbone of the donkey I struck down a thousand men."
verses.15:17: And it came about when he finished speaking, that he threw the jawbone out of his hand, and he called that place Removal of a Jawbone.
verses.15:18: And he was exceedingly thirsty, and he wept to the Lord and said, "You were well pleased with this great deliverance by the hand of Your servant, and now I will die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised."
verses.15:19: And God split open the pit that was in Jawbone, and water came out from it. And he drank, and his spirit returned and he lived. Therefore its name was called Spring of the One Who Calls, which is in Jawbone, until this day.
verses.15:20: And he judged Israel in the days of the foreigners for twenty years.
verses.16:1: And Samson went to Gaza, and saw there a woman who was a prostitute, and he went in to her.
verses.16:2: And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, "Samson has come here." And they surrounded him and lay in ambush for him all night at the gate of the city, and they kept silent all night, saying, "Until dawn breaks, and let us kill him."
verses.16:3: And Samson slept until midnight; and he arose in the middle of the night and took hold of the doors of the gate of the city along with the two posts, and lifted them up along with the bar, and placed them on his shoulders, and went up to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron, and placed them there.
verses.16:4: And it came about after this that he loved a woman in Halsorek, and her name was Delilah.
verses.16:5: And the rulers of the foreigners went up to her and said to her, "Deceive him, and see in what his great strength lies, and by what means we will prevail over him and bind him in order to humble him; and we will give you, each man, one thousand one hundred pieces of silver."
verses.16:6: And Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me in what your great strength lies, and with what you may be bound in order to be humbled."
verses.16:7: And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven moist bowstrings that have not been spoiled, then I will become weak and be like any man."
verses.16:8: And the rulers of the foreigners brought up to her seven moist bowstrings that had not been spoiled, and she bound him with them.
verses.16:9: And the ambush was sitting for her in the inner room, and she said to him, "Foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he snapped the bowstrings as if someone were to pull apart a strand of flax when it smells fire. And his strength was not known.
verses.16:10: And Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me; now then, tell me with what you may be bound."
verses.16:11: And he said to her, "If they securely bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I will become weak and be like any man."
verses.16:12: And Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and the ambush came out of the inner room, and she said, "Foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he snapped them off his arms like a thread.
verses.16:13: And Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me. Please tell me with what you may be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head with the warp and drive them with the peg into the wall, then I will be weak like any man."
verses.16:14: And it came about while he was sleeping that Delilah took the seven braids of his head and wove them into the warp and fastened them with the peg into the wall, and she said, "Foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the peg of the woven cloth from the wall.
verses.16:15: And Delilah said to Samson, "How do you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? This third time you have deceived me, and you have not told me in what your great strength lies."
verses.16:16: And it came about, when she pressed him hard with her words every day and distressed him, that he grew fainthearted to the point of dying.
verses.16:17: And he told her all his heart and said to her, "No iron has come upon my head, for I am a holy one of God from my mother's womb. If therefore I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I will become weak and be like all men."
verses.16:18: And Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, and she sent and called the rulers of the foreigners, saying, "Come up just this once more, for he has told me all his heart." And the rulers of the foreigners went up to her and brought up the silver in their hands.
verses.16:19: And Delilah put Samson to sleep on her knees, and she called a man and shaved the seven braids of his head; and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from him.
verses.16:20: And Delilah said, "Foreigners are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as once and again, and shake myself free." But he himself did not know that the Lord had departed from him.
verses.16:21: And the foreigners seized him and gouged out his eyes, and they brought him down to Gaza and shackled him with bronze shackles; and he was grinding in the prison house.
