verses.16:22: And the hair of his head began to sprout after he had been shaved.
verses.16:23: And the rulers of the foreigners gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice, and they said, "The god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
verses.16:24: And the people saw him and sang praise to their god, "Our god has delivered our enemy into our hand, the one who was devastating our land and who multiplied our wounded."
verses.16:25: And when their heart was gladdened, they said, "Call Samson out of the house of custody, and let him perform before us." And they called Samson from the prison house, and he was performing before them; and they were slapping him, and they stood him between the pillars.
verses.16:26: And Samson said to the young man who was holding his hand, "Let me go, and let me feel the pillars on which the house stands, and I will lean against them."
verses.16:27: And the house was full of the men and the women, and all the rulers of the foreigners were there; and on the roof were about seven hundred men and women looking on at the performances of Samson.
verses.16:28: And Samson wept to the Lord and said, "Adonai Lord, please remember me now and strengthen me just this once more, God, and I will repay one repayment to the foreigners for my two eyes."
verses.16:29: And Samson clasped the two pillars of the house on which the house stood, and leaned against them, and took hold of one with his right hand and one with his left hand.
verses.16:30: And Samson said, "Let my soul die with foreigners!" And he heaved with strength, and the house fell upon the rulers and upon all the people who were in it. And the dead whom Samson put to death in his death were more than those whom he put to death in his life.
verses.16:31: And his brothers and the house of his father went down and took him and went up, and they buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. And he judged Israel for twenty years.
verses.17:1: And there was a man from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Micah.
verses.17:2: And he said to his mother, "The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver that you took for yourself, and you cursed me and spoke in my ears, look, the silver is with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the Lord."
verses.17:3: And he returned the one thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother. And his mother said, "I have wholly consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image; and now I will return it to you."
verses.17:4: And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to a silversmith, and he made it into a carved image and a cast image; and it was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:5: And the house of Micah was for him a house of God; and he made an ephod and teraphim, and he filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became a priest to him.
verses.17:6: Now in those days there was no king in Israel; each man was doing what was right in his eyes.
verses.17:7: And there was a young man from Bethlehem of the clan of Judah, and he was a Levite, and this man was residing there.
verses.17:8: And the man went from Bethlehem, the city of Judah, to reside in whatever place he might find; and he came as far as Mount Ephraim and as far as the house of Micah, to make his way.
verses.17:9: And Micah said to him, "Where are you coming from?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to reside in whatever place I may find."
verses.17:10: And Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and become a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver per day and a set of garments and the things for your living."
verses.17:11: And the Levite went and began to reside with the man; and the young man was with him like one of his sons.
verses.17:12: And Micah filled the hand of the Levite, and he became a priest to him, and he was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:13: And Micah said, "Now I know that the Lord will do good to me, because the Levite has become a priest to me."
verses.18:1: In those days there was no king in Israel; and in those days the tribe of Dan was seeking an inheritance for itself to live in, because until that day no inheritance had fallen to it among the tribes of Israel.
verses.18:2: And the sons of Dan sent from their clans five men, sons of strength, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it, and they said to them, "Go and explore the land." And they came as far as Mount Ephraim, as far as the house of Micah; and they themselves spent the night there,
verses.18:3: in the house of Micah. And they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what do you have here?"
verses.18:4: And he said to them, "Micah did such and such for me, and hired me, and I became a priest for him."
verses.18:5: And they said to him, "Please inquire of God, and we will know whether our way on which we are going will prosper."
verses.18:6: And the priest said to them, "Go in peace; your way on which you are going is before the Lord."
verses.18:7: And the five men went and came to Laish; and they saw the people who were in the midst of it living in security, like the quiet custom of the Sidonians; and there is no one deterring or shaming any matter in the land, an heir squeezing from a treasury; and they are far from the Sidonians, and they have no dealings with anyone.
verses.18:8: And the five men came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and they said to their brothers, "Why are you sitting?"
verses.18:9: And they said, "Rise up and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and look, it is very good; and are you keeping quiet? Do not hesitate to go and enter to inherit the land.
verses.18:10: And when you come, you will enter to a people in security, and the land is wide, because God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
verses.18:11: And they set out from there from the clans of Dan, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men girded with weapons of battle.
verses.18:12: And they went up and encamped in Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore in that place it was called Camp of Dan, until this day; look, it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
verses.18:13: And they passed on from there to Mount Ephraim and came as far as the house of Micah.
verses.18:14: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish answered and said to their brothers, "You know that in this house there is an ephod and teraphim and a carved image and a cast image; and now know what you will do."
verses.18:15: And they turned aside there and entered into the house of the young man, the Levite, the house of Micah, and asked after his welfare.
verses.18:16: And the six hundred men who were girded with their weapons of battle were standing by the doors of the gate, those from the sons of Dan.
verses.18:17: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up,
verses.18:18: and they entered there into the house of Micah, and the priest was standing; and they took the carved image and the ephod and the teraphim and the cast image. And the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
verses.18:19: And they said to him, "Keep silent, put your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and become a father and a priest to us; is it better for you to be a priest of the house of one man, or for you to become a priest of a tribe and a house for a clan of Israel?"
verses.18:20: And the heart of the priest was made glad, and he took the ephod and the teraphim and the carved image and the cast image, and went into the midst of the people.
verses.18:21: And they turned and departed, and they put the children and the possessions and the baggage in front of them.
verses.18:22: They had gone far from the house of Micah, and look, Micah and the men who were in the houses beside the house of Micah cried out and overtook the sons of Dan.
verses.18:23: And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have cried out?"
verses.18:24: And Micah said, "Because you have taken my carved image that I made, and the priest, and have gone away; and what do I have left? And why do you say this to me, 'Why are you crying out?'"
verses.18:25: And the sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, or else men bitter in soul may confront us, and they will add a life and the life of your house."
verses.18:26: And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Micah saw that they were stronger than he was, and he returned to his house.
verses.18:27: And the sons of Dan took what Micah had made and the priest who belonged to him, and they came against Laish, against a people quiet and trusting in security; and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and they burned the city with fire.
verses.18:28: And there was no deliverer, because it is far from the Sidonians, and they have no dealings with anyone, and it is in the valley of the house of Rahab. And they built the city and settled in it,
verses.18:29: and they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; and Oulamais was the name of the city formerly.
verses.18:30: And the sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image; and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the exile of the land.
verses.18:31: And they placed for themselves the carved image that Micah had made, all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh. And it happened in those days that there was no king in Israel.
verses.19:1: And there was a Levite man residing as an outsider in the flanks of Mount Ephraim, and he took for himself a concubine wife from Bethlehem of Judah.
verses.19:2: And his concubine went away from him, and she departed from him to her father's house, to Bethlehem of Judah; and she was there for a period of four months.
verses.19:3: And her husband rose up and went after her to speak to her heart, to bring her back to himself; and his young man was with him, and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him into her father's house; and the father of the young woman saw him and rejoiced to meet him.
verses.19:4: And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, detained him, and he stayed with him for three days; and they ate and drank, and spent the night there.
verses.19:5: And it happened on the fourth day that they rose early in the morning, and he rose up to go; and the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and after this you will go."
verses.19:6: And he sat down, and the two of them ate together and drank; and the father of the young woman said to the man, "Come now, spend the night, and your heart will be made glad."
verses.19:7: And the man rose up to go; and his father-in-law urged him strongly, and he stayed and spent the night there.
verses.19:8: And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go, and the father of the young woman said, "Please strengthen your heart, and go on campaign until the day declines." And the two of them ate.
verses.19:9: And the man rose up to go, he and his concubine and his young man, and his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Look now, the day has grown weak toward evening; spend the night here, and your heart will be made glad, and tomorrow you will rise early for your way, and you will go to your tent."
verses.19:10: And the man was not willing to spend the night, and he rose up and departed, and came as far as opposite Jebus, that is, Jerusalem; and with him was a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
verses.19:11: And they came as far as Jebus; and the day had advanced very far, and the young man said to his master, "Come now, and let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusites, and let us spend the night in it."
verses.19:12: And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a foreign city in which there is no one from the sons of Israel here, and we will pass on as far as Gibeah."
verses.19:13: And he said to his young man, "Come, and let us draw near to one of the places, and we will spend the night in Gibeah or in Ramah."
verses.19:14: And they passed on and traveled, and the sun set on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
verses.19:15: And they turned aside there to go in to spend the night in Gibeah; and they went in and sat down in the open square of the city, and there was no man taking them into a house to spend the night.
verses.19:16: And look, an old man was coming from his work out of the field in the evening, and the man was from Mount Ephraim and was residing as an outsider in Gibeah, and the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.
verses.19:17: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the traveling man in the open square of the city; and the old man said, "Where are you going, and where are you coming from?"
verses.19:18: And he said to him, "We are passing along from Bethlehem of Judah to the flanks of Mount Ephraim; I am from there, and I went as far as Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to my house; and there is no man taking me into the house.
verses.19:19: Moreover, there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and for the female servant and for the young man with your servants; there is no lack of anything."
verses.19:20: And the old man said, "Peace to you; only let all your lack be upon me; only you will by no means spend the night in the open square."
verses.19:21: And he brought him into his house, and he made a place for the donkeys; and they washed their feet, and ate and drank.
verses.19:22: Now while they were making their heart glad, look, men of the city, sons of lawless men, surrounded the house, pounding on the door; and they spoke to the man, the master of the house, the old man, saying, "Bring out the man who entered into your house, so that we may know him."
verses.19:23: And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said, "No, brothers, please do not act wickedly after this man has entered into my house; do not commit this folly.
verses.19:24: Look, here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. I will bring them out, and humiliate them, and do to them what is good in your eyes; and to this man you will not do this matter of folly."
verses.19:25: And the men were not willing to listen to him; and the man seized his concubine and brought her out to them outside; and they knew her, and kept abusing her all night until morning, and they sent her away as morning rose.
verses.19:26: And the woman came toward dawn, and fell down at the door of the house where her husband was, until it grew light.
verses.19:27: And her husband rose up in the morning and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go on his way; and look, the woman, his concubine, had fallen at the doors of the house, with her hands upon the threshold.
verses.19:28: And he said to her, "Get up, and let us go." And she did not answer, because she was dead. And he took her onto the donkey, and went to his place.
verses.19:29: And he took the sword and took hold of his concubine, and dismembered her into twelve parts, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel.
verses.19:30: And it happened that everyone who saw it was saying, "Such a thing as this has not happened and has not been seen from the day the sons of Israel went up from the land of Egypt even until this day; set counsel for yourselves concerning it, and speak."
verses.20:1: And all the sons of Israel went out, and the congregation was assembled as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba and the land of Gilead, to the Lord at Mizpah.
verses.20:2: And all the tribes of Israel took their stand in the presence of the Lord in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand men on foot, drawing the sword.
verses.20:3: And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. And the sons of Israel came and said, "Speak, where did this evil happen?"
verses.20:4: And the man, the Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, "I and my concubine came to Gibeah of Benjamin to spend the night.
verses.20:5: And the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house against me by night. They wanted to murder me, and they violated my concubine, and she died.
verses.20:6: And I took hold of my concubine and cut her into pieces and sent her throughout all the territory of the inheritance of the sons of Israel, because they committed lewdness and disgrace in Israel.
verses.20:7: Look, all of you, sons of Israel, give yourselves a word and counsel there."
verses.20:8: And all the people rose up as one man, saying, "We will not go away, each man to his tent, and we will not return, each man to his house.
verses.20:9: And now this is the thing that will be done to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.
verses.20:10: However, we will take ten men for every hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred for every thousand, and a thousand for every ten thousand, to take provisions to cause them to come to Gibeah of Benjamin, to do to it according to all the disgrace that it committed in Israel."
verses.20:11: And every man of Israel was gathered to the city as one man.
verses.20:12: And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout the whole tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has happened among you?
verses.20:13: And now hand over the men, the sons of lawless ones, who are in Gibeah, and we will put them to death and purge evil from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.20:14: And the sons of Benjamin were gathered from their cities to Gibeah to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.
verses.20:15: And the sons of Benjamin were mustered on that day from the cities: twenty-three thousand, each man drawing the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were mustered as seven hundred men,
verses.20:16: chosen men from all the people, ambidextrous; all of these were slingers with stones at a hair and did not miss.
verses.20:17: And the men of Israel were mustered, besides Benjamin, four hundred thousand men drawing the sword; all of these were men of battle.
verses.20:18: And they rose up and went up to Bethel, and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said, "Who will go up for us first to battle against the sons of Benjamin?" And the Lord said, "Judah will go up first as leader."
verses.20:19: And the sons of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.
verses.20:20: And all the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin and joined battle with them at Gibeah.
verses.20:21: And the sons of Benjamin went out from Gibeah and destroyed in Israel on that day twenty-two thousand men to the ground.
verses.20:22: And the men of Israel strengthened themselves and again joined battle in the place where they had joined battle on the first day.
verses.20:23: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening, and inquired of the Lord, saying, "Should we again draw near to battle against the sons of Benjamin, our brothers?" And the Lord said, "Go up against them."
verses.20:24: And the sons of Israel approached the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
verses.20:25: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and destroyed from the sons of Israel another eighteen thousand men to the ground.
verses.20:26: And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and wept and sat there before the Lord, and fasted on that day until evening, and offered up burnt offerings and complete offerings before the Lord.
verses.20:27: For the ark of the covenant of the Lord God was there,
verses.20:28: and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, was standing before it in those days. And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord, saying, "Should we go out yet again to battle against the sons of Benjamin, our brothers, or should we hold back?" And the Lord said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands."
verses.20:29: And the sons of Israel set ambushes around Gibeah.
verses.20:30: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and joined battle against Gibeah as once and again.
verses.20:31: And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn out from the city, and they began to strike down casualties from the people as once and again on the roads, of which one goes up to Bethel and one to Gibeah in the field, about thirty men in Israel.
verses.20:32: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are falling before us as at the first." And the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw them out from the city into the roads." And they did so.
verses.20:33: And every man rose up from his place, and they joined battle at Baal-tamar. And the ambush of Israel was advancing from its place, from Maraagabe.
verses.20:34: And ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came from opposite Gibeah. And the battle was heavy, and they did not know that calamity was overtaking them.
verses.20:35: And the Lord struck Benjamin before the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed from Benjamin on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men; all of these drew the sword.
verses.20:36: And the sons of Benjamin saw that they had been struck. And the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.
verses.20:37: And as they withdrew, the ambush moved, and they spread out against Gibeah, and the ambush poured out and struck the city with the edge of the sword.
verses.20:38: And the sons of Israel had a sign with the ambush of the battle, that they should send up a signal of smoke from the city.
verses.20:39: And the sons of Israel saw that the ambush had already seized Gibeah, and they took their stand in the battle. And Benjamin began to strike down casualties among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, "Again they are surely falling before us, as in the first battle."
verses.20:40: And the signal went up more and more over the city like a pillar of smoke. And Benjamin looked behind him, and look, the complete destruction of the city went up to heaven.
verses.20:41: And the men of Israel turned back, and the men of Benjamin hurried, because they saw that evil had come upon them.
verses.20:42: And they turned before the sons of Israel toward the road of the wilderness and fled; and the battle overtook them, and those from the cities were destroying them in their midst.
verses.20:43: And they were cutting down Benjamin, and pursued him from Noua close at his heels as far as opposite Gibeah toward the rising of the sun.
verses.20:44: And eighteen thousand men fell from Benjamin; all of these were men of might.
verses.20:45: And the rest turned and were fleeing into the wilderness toward the rock of Rimmon, and the sons of Israel gleaned five thousand men from them. And the sons of Israel went down after them as far as Gedan, and struck down two thousand men of them.
verses.20:46: And all who fell from Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men drawing the sword on that day; all of these were men of might.
verses.20:47: And the rest turned and fled into the wilderness toward the rock of Rimmon, six hundred men, and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon for four months.
verses.20:48: And the sons of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the city of Methla even to the livestock and even to everything that was found in all the cities; and they burned with fire the cities that were found.
verses.21:1: And the sons of Israel swore at Mizpah, saying, "No man from among us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."
verses.21:2: And the people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before God; and they lifted up their voice and wept with a great weeping.
verses.21:3: And they said, "Why, Lord, God of Israel, has this happened, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"
verses.21:4: And it happened on the next day that the people rose early, and built an altar there, and offered up burnt offerings and complete offerings.
verses.21:5: And the sons of Israel said, "Who did not go up in the assembly from all the tribes of Israel to the Lord?" For the oath was great against those who had not gone up to the Lord, to Mizpah, saying, "He will certainly be put to death."
verses.21:6: And the sons of Israel were moved with compassion toward Benjamin their brother, and said, "One tribe has been cut off today from Israel.
verses.21:7: What shall we do for them, the remaining ones who are left, for wives? And we have sworn by the Lord not to give them any of our daughters as wives."
verses.21:8: And they said, "Which one from the tribes of Israel did not go up to the Lord, to Mizpah?" And look, no man had come to the camp from Jabesh-gilead, to the assembly.
verses.21:9: And the people were inspected, and there was not a man there from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead.
verses.21:10: And the congregation sent twelve thousand men there from the sons of might, and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword.
verses.21:11: And this you shall do: every male and every woman who has known lying with a male you shall devote to destruction, but the virgins you shall preserve alive." And they did so.
verses.21:12: And they found from among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgin women, who had not known a man by lying with a male, and they brought them to the camp, to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
verses.21:13: And the whole congregation sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin at the rock of Rimmon, and called them to peace.
verses.21:14: And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and the sons of Israel gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the daughters of Jabesh-gilead; and it pleased them so.
verses.21:15: And the people were moved with compassion for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:16: And the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for the remaining ones for wives? For women have been wiped out from Benjamin."
verses.21:17: And they said, "An inheritance of survivors belongs to Benjamin, and a tribe shall not be blotted out from Israel.
verses.21:18: For we will not be able to give them wives from our daughters, because we swore among the sons of Israel, saying, 'Cursed is the one who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"
verses.21:19: And they said, "Look now, there is a feast of the Lord in Shiloh year by year, which is north of Bethel, toward the rising of the sun, on the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
verses.21:20: And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, "Go, lie in ambush in the vineyards.
verses.21:21: And you shall watch, and look, if the daughters of the inhabitants of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves, each man a wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.21:22: And it will happen, when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with you, that we will say to them, 'Show mercy to us regarding them, because we did not take, each man his wife, in the battle, for it was not you who gave them to them; as a lot, incur guilt.'"
verses.21:23: And the sons of Benjamin did so, and took wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance, and built the cities and settled in them.
verses.21:24: And the sons of Israel departed from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his clan, and they went out from there, each man to his inheritance.
verses.21:25: Now in those days there was no king in Israel; each man would do what was right in his own sight.

notes.1:10: Codex Vaticanus reads "Kariarboxepher" (a conflation of Kiriath-arba and Kiriath-sepher) and "Ahinaan" (for MT "Ahiman"), and adds "and Hebron came out in opposition" and "offspring of Anak."
notes.1:15: Codex Vaticanus spells Caleb's daughter's name "Aza" in vv. 12-13 and "Achsah" (Greek Ascha) here, and reads "redemption" (Greek lytrosin) of water, high places, and low places where MT has "springs."
notes.1:18: Unlike MT ("Judah captured..."), the Septuagint states that Judah did not inherit these cities and includes Ashdod (Greek Azotos) and its surrounding fields; in v. 17, "Sephek" and "Anathema" correspond to MT "Zephath" and "Hormah."
notes.1:19: Instead of MT's "because they had chariots of iron," Codex Vaticanus reads "because Rechab commanded them," interpreting the Hebrew word for chariots as the proper name Rechab.
notes.1:31: Codex Vaticanus preserves several distinct place-name forms in Manasseh, Zebulun, and Asher: "Balak" (v. 27), "Kedron" and "Domana" (v. 30, MT Kitron and Nahalol), and here "Dor," "Dalaph," "Aschazei," "Chebda," "Naei," and "Ereo" (corresponding to MT Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob).
notes.1:35: Codex Vaticanus renders the place names of MT ("Mount Heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim") as "the potsherd mountain, where the bears are and where the foxes are, in the Myrtle Grove [Greek Myrsinon] and in Thalabin."
notes.2:1: The Greek translates Hebrew "Bochim" as "the Place of Weeping" (plural "Places of Weeping" in v. 5) and adds "and to Bethel and to the house of Israel."
notes.2:3: Greek "distresses" (synochas) differs from MT's "sides" (often rendered "thorns in your sides"); in v. 2, Greek also has a declarative clause ("because you did these things") instead of MT's question.
notes.2:14: In the Greek text, "wherever they went out" closes v. 14 rather than opening v. 15, and in v. 16 the clause "Yet they did not even obey the judges" closes v. 16 rather than opening v. 17.
notes.2:21: Where MT reads "when he died," Codex Vaticanus reads "in the land. And He left them," continuing directly into v. 22; in v. 23, Greek also uses the future tense "the Lord will leave."
notes.3:15: "Jemini" transliterates the Greek rendering (uion tou Iemenei) of the Hebrew expression for a Benjaminite; "ambidextrous" (amfoterodexion) is the Septuagint translation where the Hebrew describes Ehud as restricted in his right hand (left-handed).
notes.3:17: Greek asteios ("handsome" or "refined") stands where the Hebrew text describes Eglon as a very fat man.
notes.3:22: Greek flox ("flame") literally renders the Hebrew word lahav, which means both "flame" and "blade"; Codex Vaticanus also lacks the final clause found in the Hebrew ("and the refuse came out").
notes.3:26: "Seteirotha" (Seteirotha) is the distinctive Codex Vaticanus form of the place name corresponding to Seirah in the Hebrew; the preceding clause "and there was no one paying attention to him" is likewise a Septuagint addition.
notes.3:31: "Dinach" (Deinach) is the distinctive Codex Vaticanus name for Shamgar's father (Hebrew: Anath); Greek also reads "foreigners" (allofylous, the standard Septuagint term for the Philistines in Judges) and "plowshare of the oxen" (arotropodi ton boon, Hebrew: oxgoad).
notes.4:5: "Bama" (Bama) is the distinctive Codex Vaticanus place name where other witnesses and the Hebrew read Ramah.
notes.4:7: Codex Vaticanus includes the preposition epi ("against") before Sisera, yielding an intransitive military sense for epaxo ("march" or "advance"), whereas other Greek witnesses and the Hebrew omit it ("draw Sisera to you").
notes.4:8: The closing clause "for I do not know the day on which the Lord prospers the angel with me" is a notable Septuagint addition absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.4:9: Codex Vaticanus reads "from Kedesh" (ek Kades), repeated in 4:10, where the Hebrew has "to Kedesh."
notes.4:11: "Jobab" (Iobab) is the Septuagint name form corresponding to Hebrew Hobab, and "the oak of the greedy" (dryos pleonektounton) translates the Hebrew place name Zaanannim as a Greek participle.
notes.4:17: "Heber the companion" (Chaber hetairou) reflects a Codex Vaticanus doublet that both transliterates the name Heber and translates its Hebrew root meaning ("companion" or "ally").
notes.5:1: The Vaticanus text reads the imperfect ἦσαν with λέγοντες ('were saying'); in uncial script without iota subscript this is identical to ᾖσαν ('sang'), which reflects the Hebrew.
notes.5:2: Codex Vaticanus uniquely reads ἀκουσιασθῆναι ('were unwilling'), contrasting with ἑκουσιαζόμενοι ('offer themselves willingly') in v. 9; ἀπεκαλύφθη ἀποκάλυμμα literally means 'a revelation was revealed' (or 'an uncovering was uncovered').
notes.5:5: The Vaticanus phrase Κυρίου Ἐλωεί ('the Lord Eloi') retains an untranslated transliteration of the Hebrew title Elohei ('God') alongside 'the Lord'.
notes.5:16: Vaticanus reads ἀγγέλων ('messengers' or 'angels'), likely an inner-Greek corruption of ἀγελῶν ('herds/flocks'); διγομίας literally denotes a double pack-load.
notes.5:30: Οἰκτείρμων οἰκτειρήσει ('a compassionate one will show compassion') reflects the Greek translator reading the Hebrew root r-ḥ-m as 'mercy/compassion' rather than 'womb/maiden'.
notes.6:11: Vaticanus reads 'Ephrathah' (Ἐφραθά) where the Hebrew has Ophrah, and divides 'the Abiezrite' into 'father of Esdri' (πατρὸς τοῦ Ἐσδρεί; cf. v. 24 and 'Abiezer' in v. 34).
notes.6:13: Ἐν ἐμοί ('In me', also in v. 15) is a hyper-literal Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew particle of entreaty bî ('please' or 'pardon me').
notes.6:17: Vaticanus reads σήμερον ('today') rather than 'a sign' (σημεῖον), linking the conditional clause directly to the request in v. 18.
notes.6:26: Μαουέκ ('Mauek') is an untranslated Vaticanus transliteration of the Hebrew word for 'stronghold'.
notes.6:31: Codex Vaticanus makes 'Gideon son of Joash' the speaker here rather than Joash, and in v. 32 reads 'he called it Arbaal' (Ἀρβάαλ, for Hebrew Jerubbaal) with passive 'was torn down'.
notes.6:34: Vaticanus reads ἐφοβήθη ('was afraid') where the Hebrew means 'was summoned/called out'.
notes.7:1: Codex Vaticanus transliterates the Hebrew phrase 'the hill of Moreh' as a single place name, Gabaathamora.
notes.7:11: Codex Vaticanus reads 'of the fifty' (ton pentekonta), interpreting the Hebrew term for 'armed men' (hamushim) as the similar-looking numeral 'fifty' (hamishim).
notes.7:19: The emphatic Greek phrase 'they indeed roused the guards' literally renders a Hebrew idiom meaning 'they had just stationed the guards,' and 'shook out' (exetinaxan) preserves the Greek verb where verse 20 uses 'shattered.'
notes.7:22: Codex Vaticanus preserves the distinct place names Bethseedta Garagatha and Abomeoula where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Beth-shittah toward Zererah and Abel-meholah.
notes.7:25: Codex Vaticanus retains the distinct place name Bethera in verse 24 (Hebrew Beth-barah) and transliterates Hebrew 'rock of Oreb' and 'winepress of Zeeb' as the place names Sur and Jakephzeph.
notes.8:7: Codex Vaticanus leaves the rare Hebrew term barqanim (likely briers or threshing-sledges) untranslated as 'habarkenein' (retaining the Hebrew definite article) and in verse 16 as 'barakeneim.'
notes.8:11: Codex Vaticanus preserves the distinct place names Nabai and Jegebal (Hebrew Nobah and Jogbehah); in verse 10 it likewise reads 'foreigners' (allophylon) where the Hebrew reads 'sons of the east.'
notes.8:13: Codex Vaticanus repeats 'of the battle' (tes parataxeos), reading 'from above the battle of Heres' where other witnesses and the Hebrew read 'by the ascent of Heres.'
notes.8:26: Codex Vaticanus gives the weight as one thousand five hundred gold pieces, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads one thousand seven hundred.
notes.8:27: Codex Vaticanus reads the distinct city name Ephrathah (also in verse 32) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Ophrah.
notes.8:33: Codex Vaticanus translates the divine title Baal-berith as 'a covenant with Baal,' and in verse 32 reads that Gideon died 'in his city' rather than the Hebrew 'in a good old age.'
notes.9:5: Codex Vaticanus reads Ephrathah where the Hebrew MT reads Ophrah.
notes.9:6: Codex Vaticanus reads "house of Beth-maalon" (also in 9:20; Hebrew MT "Beth-millo") and "the found oak of the station," a double rendering reflecting Hebrew "oak of the pillar."
notes.9:26: Codex Vaticanus names this figure Gilead son of Jobel throughout the chapter (spelled Gaad in 9:28), where the Hebrew MT reads Gaal son of Ebed.
notes.9:27: Codex Vaticanus transliterates Hebrew hillulim (a harvest thanksgiving festival or festival offerings) as helloulim, reads "brought them" for MT "entered," and reads "spoke" (Greek eipon) where MT has "drank" (likely from Greek epion).
notes.9:37: Codex Vaticanus adds "toward the sea" before "from next to the navel of the land" and leaves the place name Elon-maonemin (Hebrew "Diviners' Oak") untranslated.
notes.9:46: Codex Vaticanus renders Hebrew tsariach ("stronghold" or "crypt") as "assembly place" (Greek syneleusis, also in 9:49) and gives the name Beth-er-berith (MT "house of El-berith"), which it also inserts in 9:50.
notes.9:48: Codex Vaticanus reads Mount Hermon where the Hebrew MT reads Mount Zalmon.
notes.10:1: Greek renders Hebrew dodo as "his paternal uncle" rather than as the proper name Dodo found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:4: The Codex Vaticanus Greek text reads "thirty-two" three times here (versus "thirty" in the Hebrew Masoretic Text) and translates the place name Havvoth-jair as "Settlements of Jair."
notes.10:5: Greek reads "Ramnon" (Ῥαμνών), an LXX-distinct proper name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Kamon."
notes.10:6: Greek reads "Arad" (Ἀράδ), an LXX-distinct proper name where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Aram" (Syria).
notes.10:12: Greek reads "Midian" (Μαδιάμ), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Maon."
notes.10:17: Greek translates the Hebrew place name Mizpah literally as "the watchtower" (σκοπιά) here and in 11:29, whereas 11:11 and 11:34 transliterate it as Mizpah (Μασσηφά).
notes.11:1: Greek describes Jephthah as "exalted in strength" (ἐπηρμένος δυνάμει) and makes his mother the subject of the final clause ("who bore Jephthah to Gilead").
notes.11:2: Greek reads "a courtesan" (ἑταίρας) rather than "another" (ἑτέρας, corresponding to the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "another woman").
notes.11:16: Greek transliterates Hebrew Suf as "Siph" (Σείφ) in "Sea of Siph" rather than translating it as "the Red Sea."
notes.11:24: Greek reads "Hamos" (Ἁμώς), a Codex Vaticanus variant form of the deity Chemosh (Hebrew Kemosh).
notes.11:26: Greek reads "its territories" (for Hebrew "its villages"), "the land of Aroer," and "beside the Jordan" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "beside the Arnon").
notes.11:27: Greek uses the emphatic kaige idiom ἐγώ εἰμι (literally "I am") before a finite verb here and in 11:35 (and with a noun in 11:37) to render emphatic Hebrew "I," translated here as "I myself."
notes.11:33: Greek reads "Arnon" (Ἀρνών) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "Minnith," and adds "in number" before "twenty cities."
notes.12:1: The Greek renders the Hebrew directional term as "to the north" rather than the town name Zaphon.
notes.12:4: The Greek makes "the survivors of Ephraim" the subject of "said," whereas the Hebrew is commonly read as "Fugitives of Ephraim are you, Gilead."
notes.12:6: Codex Vaticanus translates the Hebrew test word Shibboleth by its literal meaning, "Ear of grain" (Greek Stachys), rather than transliterating its sound.
notes.12:7: Codex Vaticanus reads "sixty years," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "six years."
notes.12:12: The Greek uses the same name form (Ailom) for both the judge and his burial place, corresponding to Elon and Aijalon in the Hebrew.
notes.13:2: Codex Vaticanus reads the distinct place name "Saral" here (contrast Zorah in 13:25).
notes.13:8: Greek "en emoi" (literally "in me") is a literal rendering of the Hebrew entreaty particle "bi" ("please"), and "Kyrie Adonaie" combines "Lord" with a transliteration of Hebrew Adonai.
notes.13:14: Codex Vaticanus renders Hebrew strong drink with a double phrase ("sikera methysma," "strong intoxicating drink") and reads the masculine/neuter pronoun "auto" ("him") rather than "her."
notes.13:19: Greek "diechorisen poiesai" (literally "separated/distinguished to do") reflects a literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for acting wondrously.
notes.13:25: Codex Vaticanus reads "to go out with him" (Greek synekporeuesthai), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "to stir him."
notes.14:1: Here and in verses 3-4 the Greek uses "allophyloi" ("foreigners"), whereas verse 2 uses "Phylistieim" ("Philistines").
notes.14:4: The Greek reads "vengeance" (ekdikesis) rather than "an occasion" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.14:8: Here and in verse 9 the Greek reads "mouth" (stoma) rather than "body" or "carcass" as in the Hebrew.
notes.14:14: Codex Vaticanus frames Samson's riddle as an explicit question beginning with "What" rather than a declarative statement.
notes.14:18: The Greek reads "before the sun rose" (compare also "on the fourth day" in verse 15), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "before the sun went down" (and "on the seventh day" in verse 15).
notes.15:3: The Greek text consistently refers to the Philistines as allophyloi ("foreigners") throughout Judges.
notes.15:15: Codex B describes the donkey's jawbone as "cast aside" (ekrerimmenen, discarded), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "fresh."
notes.15:16: Codex B reads "I utterly wiped them out" (exaleiphon exeleipsa autous), diverging from the Hebrew wordplay "heaps upon heaps."
notes.15:17: Greek translates the Hebrew place name Ramath-lehi as Anairesis siagonos ("Removal of a Jawbone," also capable of meaning "Destruction of a Jawbone"), paralleling the translation of Lehi as "Jawbone" in vv. 14 and 19 (transcribed Leuei in v. 9).
notes.15:18: Codex B reads "wept" (eklausen, also in 16:28) rather than "called," and "were well pleased with" (eudokesas) where the Hebrew text reads "have given."
notes.16:4: Codex B fuses the Hebrew phrase "the Valley of Sorek" (nahal Soreq) into a single proper name, Halsorek (Halsorech).
notes.16:7: Codex B reads "that have not been spoiled" (me diephtharmenais, also in v. 8), reflecting a different sense of the Hebrew root than "that have not been dried."
notes.16:13: Codex B preserves the fuller wording in vv. 13-14 about driving the woven braids into the wall with a peg and becoming weak, which is shorter in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.16:17: Codex B reads "iron" (sideros) where the Hebrew has "razor," and renders Hebrew "Nazirite to God" as "a holy one of God" (hagios theou).
notes.16:27: Codex B states "about seven hundred" men and women on the roof, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "about three thousand."
notes.17:2: Codex B reads active "that you took for yourself" and "you cursed me," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads passive "that were taken from you" and "you uttered a curse."
notes.17:5: Codex B reads "the house of Micah" where the Hebrew has "the man Micah"; "filled the hand" (also in v. 12) is a literal idiom for consecrating or installing someone as a priest.
notes.17:10: Codex B reads singular "per day" (eis hemeran), where the Hebrew has plural "for the days" (idiomatically "per year").
notes.17:11: Codex B renders the Hebrew verb as "began" (erxato) rather than "agreed" or "was content," reflecting a homonymous Hebrew root.
notes.18:7: The Greek idiom 'in security' literally reads 'in hope' (used in the Septuagint for living securely). The phrase 'deterring or shaming any matter' doubles the rendering of the underlying Hebrew, and 'an heir squeezing from a treasury' reflects the Codex Vaticanus rendering of an obscure Hebrew phrase concerning an oppressive ruler.
notes.18:25: The Codex Vaticanus Greek reads 'confront us' (first person) and 'add a life' (rendering Hebrew 'gather/lose' as 'add'), differing from the Hebrew text's 'fall upon you, and you lose your life.'
notes.18:28: The Greek reads 'the house of Rahab,' an LXX-distinct form corresponding to the place name Beth-rehob in the Hebrew text.
notes.18:29: The Greek proper name Oulamais fuses the Hebrew conjunction and city name ('however, Laish') into a single former name for the city.
notes.18:30: Codex Vaticanus reads 'Manasseh,' agreeing with the Masoretic Hebrew reading (with its suspended letter nun), whereas other Greek witnesses such as Codex Alexandrinus read 'Moses.'
notes.19:2: The Codex Vaticanus Greek reads 'went away from him,' whereas Codex Alexandrinus reads 'became angry with him' and the Hebrew text reads 'played the prostitute against him.'
notes.19:8: The Codex Vaticanus Greek literally reads 'go on campaign' (strateuson), likely an ancient scribal spelling error for 'linger' (stranggeuson), matching the Hebrew text.
notes.19:18: The Greek reads 'to my house,' differing from the Masoretic Hebrew text's 'to the house of the Lord.'
notes.19:21: The Codex Vaticanus Greek reads 'made a place for the donkeys,' whereas the Hebrew text reads 'gave fodder to the donkeys.'
notes.19:28: The Greek explicitly states 'because she was dead,' a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:6: Greek zema is a transliteration of Hebrew zimmah ("lewdness, depravity"), paired here with apoptoma ("moral fall, disgrace").
notes.20:15: Codex Vaticanus reads "twenty-three thousand" (against twenty-six thousand in the Hebrew text) and in v. 16 describes the seven hundred men of Gibeah as "ambidextrous" (Greek amphoterodexioi) without repeating the number seven hundred.
notes.20:26: Greek teleias ("complete offerings") renders Hebrew shelamim ("peace offerings") etymologically from the root for completeness; in vv. 27-28 Codex Vaticanus places Israel's inquiry after the notice concerning the ark and Phinehas.
notes.20:33: Maraagabe is the Greek transliteration as a proper name of the Hebrew expression ma'areh-geba ("clearing/meadow of Geba").
notes.20:43: Noua is a Septuagint-distinct place name corresponding to Hebrew menuchah ("resting place" or "with ease"), and the Greek reads "cutting down" rather than "surrounding."
notes.20:45: Gedan is the Septuagint form of the place name corresponding to Gidom in the Hebrew text, and Codex Vaticanus reads "went down after them" rather than "pursued closely."
notes.20:48: Methla is a Septuagint-distinct city name reflecting a Greek rendering of the difficult Hebrew phrase meaning "from an inhabited city" or "from city, people."
notes.21:4: The Codex Vaticanus Greek reads teleias ("complete [offerings]"), rendering Hebrew shelamim (traditionally "peace offerings") by its root sense of wholeness or completeness, rather than eirenikas ("peace offerings") as in Codex Alexandrinus.
notes.21:11: The explicit command to preserve the virgins alive and the notice "And they did so" are present in the Septuagint Greek but absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.21:14: Codex Vaticanus reads "and it pleased them so" (kai eresen autois houtos), contrasting with the Hebrew ("yet there were not enough for them") and Codex Alexandrinus ("and it did not suffice for them so"), likely reflecting an early Greek scribal shift from ouk erkesen ("did not suffice") to eresen ("pleased").
notes.21:22: The Codex Vaticanus Greek reads "with you" (rather than the Hebrew "with us") and ends with the obscure "as a lot, incur guilt" (hos kleros plemmelesate), likely an early Greek corruption of "at this time [lit. as the season], you will incur guilt" (hos kairos plemmelesete; cf. Hebrew "now you would be guilty").
notes.21:25: Codex Vaticanus reads "in his own sight" (enopion autou, lit. "before himself") rather than "in his own eyes" as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text and Codex Alexandrinus.
